gen-gf-autour-one-gf-menbere: Menbere reads tall and rolled, like cord stacked in neat rows. Autour One is the showier one, its wire-like strokes holding one constant width, while the body simply keeps text moving along.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-mitr: Mitr sits low and compact, with barely any gap between its lowercase and its capitals. Mitr also carries a friendly, contemporary ease, and Autour One's bold, constant-width curves give the pair its strongest single quality: a confident, bendy-wire punch.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-momo-trust-display: Autour One looks like a wire bent into signage, bold and expressive with a channel leading into each round letter. Momo Trust Display follows with a generous x-height and loosely drifting letters, which gives the heading room to be loud.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-mukta: Mukta reads upright and tidy, its small letters standing tall. If Autour One were shrunk down, its pen-tip outlines would lose their swagger, while this plain sans stays comfortable at any size.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-mukta-mahee: Autour One draws every line at a constant width, bold and expressive. Mukta Mahee brings chunky, tall lowercase letters that feel approachable, so a long page would read friendly and steady rather than showy.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-mukta-malar: Autour One looks like bent wire, bold and monoline, with a clear channel into each round letter. Mukta Malar tucks its ascenders short and stays neutral, so the pair's strongest quality is a loud heading over a quiet, compact text.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-mukta-vaani: Mukta Vaani has a high-waisted lowercase and a contemporary, tidy manner. Autour One does best at drafting-pen outlines of one nib width and bold attitude, while the body does its best work simply carrying text.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-narnoor: Autour One's wire-bent s curves never thin at the spine, giving every line a bold, expressive punch. Narnoor answers with short ascenders above big bowls, a sturdy, businesslike text face.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-display: Expressive and bold, Autour One draws straight-edged strokes of constant width, with a minimal step from capital to lowercase. Noto Sans Display does the quieter job, its big, tall middle zone keeping words approachable.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-play: Play reads compact, with little height difference between its cases and a faint stroke contrast that keeps it feeling alive. Over a long page that slight variation keeps things moving, while Autour One stays fixed-pen bold.
